01 / Frontier GTM

A working thesis,
backed by builds.

Frontier GTM combines agent-led processes for coverage, LLMs for semantic understanding, network analysis for market structure, and people for judgment.

  1. 01

    Agent-led systems and processes

    Well-structured, repeatable agent workflows beat vibecoded apps that never become part of the work. Scheduled and always-on agents increase coverage; people stay in the loop for judgment.

    See supporting builds ↓
  2. 02

    The semantic power of LLMs

    Start with where the useful text lives — social posts, job descriptions, websites and calls. Let agents plan collection and enrichment, then give power users control over querying, qualification and angles.

    See supporting builds ↓
  3. 03

    Network analysis

    Map the buyer ecosystem, find communities, central nodes and bridges, then search the network semantically. The output is sharper targeting, broader market coverage and tactics grounded in real structure.

    See supporting builds ↓

03 / How I work

Strategy with dirty hands.

The useful answer is usually sitting between the customer conversation and the data model.

  1. 01

    Touch the raw material

    Read the transcripts. Open the search-terms report. Take the calls. Abstractions are earned after contact.

  2. 02

    Ship the smallest live loop

    A working v1 creates better information than a memo. Get the signal moving, then industrialise what proves useful.

  3. 03

    Build leverage that compounds

    Skills, tools and knowledge should make the next job cheaper. I design operating systems, not isolated automations.

04 / About

Growth is a product problem with a commercial deadline.

I’ve led go-to-market across B2B, marketplace, consumer and creator products — from first-employee scrappiness at Timewith to the post-administration turnaround at Disciple, where I became AI Czar.

I’m strongest where the problem crosses boundaries: the positioning needs the sales calls, the targeting needs a data pipeline, or the growth idea needs someone willing to open the codebase.
